proves: each of the sixteen blend modes composites its own way, over a backdrop that has both a dark half and a light one
checkable: 382x148 on white. Seventeen 56x40 cells, six per row at x=8, 70, 132, 194, 256 and 318, rows at y=8, 54 and 100. Each holds a 36x24 source of #4090c0 over a ramp running left to right from #181838 to #f0e0a0. Read the source at two points: x+14 (the backdrop is dark there) and x+42 (it is light). All seventeen cells hash differently, which is the first thing to check; the pairs below are what says each is the RIGHT mode rather than merely a different one.
why_the_backdrop_is_a_ramp: on a flat backdrop several of these modes collapse onto each other and a cell would prove far less than it looks. multiply and darken agree wherever the backdrop is lighter than the source; screen and lighten agree wherever it is darker. The ramp puts both halves of each pair inside one cell, which is why the two sample points matter more than the cell hash - `darken` reading 64,76,83 on the left and 64,144,135 on the right is the mode choosing per channel, and a flat cell would have shown only one of those.
why_a_control_with_no_source: `normal` has to be read against something. A mode that drew nothing at all would look like a mode that let the backdrop through, and the two are only distinguishable beside a cell where nothing was drawn: the control reads 80,76,83 where `normal` reads 64,144,192.
what_is_not_pinned: the exact composited values are Skia's arithmetic, but blend modes are EXACT rather than approximate - each is a formula on channels, not a filter kernel - so unlike a blur these numbers are a reference another engine should reproduce. Chrome-answerable, and worth asking for.
status: measured from the committed image. Fourteen of these sixteen modes were drawn by nothing in this project before this fixture; the showcase draws multiply and difference.
